intent: Interact with and test local web applications using browser automation to verify frontend functionality, debug UI behavior, capture screenshots and inspect browser logs.
steps: Determine whether the target is static HTML or a dynamic web application
For static HTML, read the markup to identify selectors then write an automation script
For dynamic applications, confirm whether the application server is already running
When the server is not running, use a server lifecycle helper to start required services before automation
Apply reconnaissance-then-action: navigate, wait for network idle, inspect rendered DOM or capture screenshot, identify selectors, then execute actions
Write automation scripts using a headless browser in synchronous mode
Wait for dynamic content to finish loading before DOM inspection on single-page applications
Use descriptive selectors and explicit waits for elements or conditions
Capture console logs and screenshots when debugging or evidence is required
Close browser resources when automation completes
Consult bundled helper scripts with help output before reading their source; treat helpers as black boxes when sufficient
invariants: Do not inspect dynamic DOM before content has settled
Prefer helper scripts for complex server lifecycle over reimplementing them
Evidence must reflect rendered state, not assumptions from source markup alone
